ak_blackerby_ice.blurb: Blackerby is a small ice area on the steep slope above Twin Lakes in the Lemon Creek valley, close to Juneau. It holds six routes, five of them around WI4 and one harder at WI5, so it suits climbers already comfortable on steep water ice rather than beginners. Walk-ins are short and avalanche exposure is low. The ice can be good, but it forms more slowly than at some other Juneau venues and often stays wet after a cold snap. Reaching the amphitheater at the heart of the area takes a short, easier entrance pitch, and warm weather makes the approach under it hazardous. The longest line on the ridge is a multi-pitch climb at the north end.

ak_gulkana_boulder.blurb: Gulkana Boulder is a single large boulder on the moraine below the Gulkana Glacier, in the Delta Range of the eastern Alaska Range. It sits roughly a quarter hour up the moraine from the end of the road, in a glacial landscape with good camping nearby. It has six problems, running from an easy V0 up to a hard V5-6, with most in the V2 to V5 range. Expect a quiet day with the glacier as a backdrop; bring pads, since there is only one block to work.

ak_o_malley_peak_3.blurb: O'Malley Peak is a Chugach Front Range summit above 5,000 feet inside Chugach State Park, about a dozen miles southeast of downtown Anchorage. It offers alpine rock, scrambling and a little winter ice. Of the six climbs here, most are trad or alpine lines, ranging from fourth-class terrain up to about 5.9, plus one moderate ice route. The west buttress has many lines, with tricky route-finding in the middle and easier fifth-class climbing on the right side. It makes a natural next step after the nearby Wedge for climbers who want mountain-style outings close to town. The easiest way up is a class 2 hike.

ak_lower_hunter_2.blurb: Lower Hunter is the lower stretch of the Hunter Creek drainage in South Central Alaska, where a handful of water-ice climbs form within a short walk upstream of a bridge. All six routes are ice: one at WI2, three at WI3 and two at WI4, so it is a fair choice for climbers moving up from moderates as well as those after a steeper pillar. The best-known line is a big ice fall reached by hiking up the riverbed, and parties below should watch for ice knocked down from above. The valley is secluded and the ice sits at low elevation.

ak_hole_in_the_wall_2.blurb: Hole In The Wall is an ice amphitheater just outside the mouth of Keystone Canyon near Valdez, a cluster of ice formations with lines from friendly moderates to technical steeps. It has six routes, split evenly between WI3, WI4 and WI5, and a couple run to two pitches. The walk follows the riverbed upstream for about a mile, which can be a quick stroll on packed snow or a slow post-hole in deep snow, so skis or snowshoes help. Ice screws are the protection, and descents are by rappel from alders or threads.

ak_incinerator_crag.blurb: Incinerator Crag is a small roadside wall on the highway north of Skagway, beyond the Black Lakes, with its climbs on the back of a roadcut. It is better known for difficulty than volume: six climbs mix two sport routes at 5.11, two trad lines (one at 5.9 and one very hard crack through a roof) and two boulder problems from V3 to V6. This is not a beginner stop. The crag is wide enough that more lines look possible, and its north face is where the bolted routes go.

ak_glacier_creek_bouldering.blurb: Glacier Creek Bouldering is a small collection of boulders in the Glacier Creek drainage of the Hatcher Pass area, in South Central Alaska. Reaching it means following the creek up past several benches toward the old mine ruins. It has five problems: three boulder problems from a very easy VB up to a hard V6, with a V2 between, plus two short crack climbs at roughly 5.9 and 5.10. The rock has a pebbly texture that makes some moves a wrestle.

ak_upper_crack_in_the_woods.blurb: Upper Crack in the Woods is the left-hand of two small crags tucked beside the Seward Highway south of Anchorage, reached by taking the left branch of a short trail under trees along a creek. It has five routes, from 5.7 to 5.10, mostly trad with one top-rope line, so it offers a modest range for climbers building gear skills. The setting is a quiet, sheltered spot off the road, usually warmer than the highway, though bugs can be intense in season.
